summary.headline: Nuvoco Q2 FY27: volume up 9% YoY and revenue up ~14%, but energy cost rose ~INR90/ton QoQ; Q3 fuel guided to INR1.8/mn kcal from INR1.59.
summary.overview: Management described a challenging quarter driven by a renewed Middle East escalation, petcoke and domestic coal price spikes, and monsoon disruption in the East. Volume grew 9% YoY, revenue about 14% and EBITDA about 11%, supported by premiumization at a record 45% and trade mix of 75%. Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal in Q2, and management guided Q3 to INR1.8 with about INR100-120/ton net cost inflation QoQ, offset by an October price hike of about INR20/ton. Vadraj's Surat grinding unit (2 MTPA) was commissioned in late September, and net debt rose above INR5,000 crore on working capital and capex, with a guided return to 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters.

segments.name: Gujarat (Vadraj / Surat & Kutch)
segments.commentary: Surat 2 MTPA grinding unit commissioned in late September; running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised, targeting 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28. Kutch clinker line expected in Q4 FY27, with jetty operational by first week of December.

segments.name: North
segments.commentary: Strong volume growth in Q2 per management. Around 1 million tons of cement capacity to be released from Rajasthan from Q4 for North sales, as Surat supplies Gujarat.

segments.name: East
segments.commentary: Erratic monsoon weighed on demand in Q2; East expansion deferred from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28. Price hike of about INR20/ton in trade and non-trade taken in October.

guidance_outlook: Q3 FY27 fuel cost guided at INR1.8 per million kcal vs INR1.59 in Q2, adding ~INR70-80/ton energy cost QoQ; Q4 could add a further INR70-80/ton in a worst case.
Q3 FY27 net cost inflation guided at INR100-120/ton QoQ (energy ~INR70-80, packing bags ~INR20, busy-season surcharge waiver ~INR10), offset by ~INR20/ton price increase taken in October.
Industry demand expected at ~8% growth in H2 FY27; company guides 8-9% blended volume growth across North, West and East.
FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore spent in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2); FY28 capex INR800-900 crore.
Net debt expected to return to around March 2026 levels by end FY27; 2-2.5x net debt/EBITDA in the next 4-6 quarters, and below 2x once Vadraj volumes scale.
Surat incremental costs of ~INR30-40 crore expected in Q3 (interest and depreciation), partly above and below EBITDA.
Vadraj/Gujarat EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India EBITDA per ton around FY29 (possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29).
Company targets 35 MTPA cement capacity by FY28.
capex_capacity: Surat (Vadraj) 2 MTPA grinding unit at Limla, Surat commissioned late September 2026; ~3,500-3,600 tons/day peak output against ~5,500 tons/day capacity.
Kutch clinker/grinding project on track: phased operations from Q3 FY27, clinker line December, Kutch clinker to Surat via barge once jetty is operational.
Viramgam (Sachana) bulk cement terminal with railway siding under construction; INR50 crore spend planned in H2 FY27.
East debottlenecking delayed from Q3-Q4 FY27 to Q1-Q2 FY28 to prioritise Vadraj cash flow and management bandwidth.
CleanMax agreement for 46.4 MW wind-solar hybrid project in Rajasthan, expected ~100 million units/year.
demand_pricing: Industry demand grew in Q2 but varied regionally; monsoon disrupted the East while low-rainfall regions performed better. Prices did not improve as expected in Q2.

Price action: non-trade up ~INR20-25/ton in North after 15 September, trade cut INR5-7/ton in North in late September, then ~INR20/ton increases in non-trade (North and East) and trade (East) in October.
Premium product mix at 45%; Duraguard Microfiber and Concreto Uno each crossed 1 million ton volumes, with Concreto Uno reaching it in under 18 months.
Management expects post-Diwali demand pickup and believes price increases will hold through the balance of the year.
Management sees 5% demand impact only if back-to-back adverse monsoon or drought years occur; assumes this does not happen in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What was average fuel cost in Q2 and what is the spot impact at petcoke near $187?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel cost rose from INR1.52 to INR1.59 per million kcal (energy ~INR1,080/ton vs INR1,005 in Q1). Q3 is guided at INR1.8, adding ~INR70-80/ton, with petcoke covered for Q3 and Q4 through mid-February.

qa_highlights.question: What is the overall Q3 vs Q2 cost outlook and how will it be offset?
qa_highlights.answer: Net cost inflation of INR100-120/ton: energy +INR70-80, packing +INR20, raw materials ~+INR10, offset by ~INR20/ton price increase plus fixed-cost leverage from higher volumes.

qa_highlights.question: What is Surat's utilisation and run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Running at ~1.5 MTPA annualised; target 2 MTPA in Q4 FY27 with 50-60% utilisation in Q4 and 70-75% in FY28, as Kutch grinding is not available in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What are the capex plans and timelines?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex ~INR1,200 crore (INR780 crore in H1, ~INR420 crore in H2, of which INR1,000 crore for Vadraj); FY28 INR800-900 crore. East expansion delayed 6-8 months to FY28 H1.

qa_highlights.question: How will net debt evolve and what is the target?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt crossed INR5,000 crore (INR200 crore working capital build plus capex). Expected to return to March 2026 levels by end FY27, and to hover at 2-2.5x EBITDA over 4-6 quarters, with the long-term target below 2x.

qa_highlights.question: Why did interest expense fall and will it continue?
qa_highlights.answer: Borrowing costs for Surat were capitalised until commercial operations started in late September; interest and depreciation will rise QoQ from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What is the tax rate outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 reported tax rate 41.6% because MAT credit is unavailable under the old regime; the company will decide on regime transition within 3-4 months and share the implications.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Vadraj EBITDA per ton outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Gujarat and Western Maharashtra EBITDA per ton expected to match Nuvoco's all-India level in year 3 (FY29, possibly FY28 Q4 to Q1 FY29), subject to cost inflation being offset by prices.

risks_watch: Petcoke prices near $190 with potential to exceed $200/ton; full impact of high-cost petcoke expected from March 2027 onwards.
Domestic coal auction premiums and rake shortages; linkage coal supply expected to ease from early November.
Price hikes must hold post-Diwali; any reversal would erode the expected Q3 benefit.
Surat clinker is currently sourced from Chhattisgarh and Chittor at high cost until Kutch clinker starts; the Q3 to Q4 margin dent was not quantified on the call.
Net debt at above INR5,000 crore vs the INR3,500-4,000 crore comfort range; deleveraging depends on H2 working capital release.
Tax regime transition decision pending; affects tax rate from FY28.
Geopolitical developments (Middle East) remain a watch item.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operational execution and pricing actions, and candid about the cost shock. Management was evasive on specifics where variables were still moving: Q4 fuel cost, Surat clinker delta and regional growth splits were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: Overall, we are looking at as a company, from the current run rate of 1.5 annualized tons per annualized volume, we'll go to 2 million tons in Q4 this year.
And once the monsoon ends and the festival ends, I think construction activity will pick up speed going forward.
So, the average INR20 price increase should totally defray the cost increase, and we'll have a delta benefit in realization in Q3 versus Q2.
